entities.name: atom
entities.description: Matter structure whose internal electrons, energy levels, and spectra are modeled by quantum mechanics.

entities.name: Bell inequality
entities.description: Mathematical constraint on correlations implied by local hidden-variable theories.

entities.name: black-body radiation
entities.description: Radiation characterized by a curve of light intensity across frequencies from hot objects.

entities.name: classical physics
entities.description: Physics describing matter and energy at scales familiar from human experience.

entities.name: Copenhagen interpretation
entities.description: Interpretation stating that before measurement, statements about a particle's properties are completely meaningless.

entities.name: correspondence principle
entities.description: Requirement that quantum theory converge to classical limits at macroscopic scales.

entities.name: Dirac wave equation
entities.description: Relativistic wave equation for electrons that incorporates relativity and predicts antimatter.

entities.name: double-slit experiment
entities.description: Experiment in which particles or waves passing through two slits produce an interference pattern.

entities.name: eigenstate
entities.description: State in which an object has a definite value for a specified property or measurement.

entities.name: eigenvalue
entities.description: Definite value associated with an eigenstate of a quantum property.

entities.name: electron
entities.description: Corpuscular particle whose properties and behavior are central to the quantum phenomena described.

entities.name: electron microscope
entities.description: Technological application of quantum mechanics.

entities.name: energy quantum
entities.description: Discrete unit of energy proposed for light and used to explain black-body radiation and the photoelectric effect.

entities.name: interference pattern
entities.description: Pattern of alternating light and dark bands produced by wave interference and reproduced by quantum particles statistically.

entities.name: laser
entities.description: Technological application of quantum mechanics.

entities.name: local hidden-variable theory
entities.description: Theory in which measurement outcomes depend on hidden variables local to each separated particle.

entities.name: magnetic resonance imaging
entities.description: Technological application of quantum mechanics.

entities.name: many-worlds interpretation
entities.description: Interpretation describing a multiverse containing every possible universe.

entities.name: Pauli exclusion principle
entities.description: Principle that two electrons in an atom cannot have the same set of quantum numbers.

entities.name: photoelectric effect
entities.description: Ejection of electrons from a metal surface when illuminated, with electron number depending on light intensity and velocity on frequency.

entities.name: photon
entities.description: Quantum or smallest observable particle of the electromagnetic field.

entities.name: principle of complementarity
entities.description: Principle that a quantum system displays wave-like or particle-like properties according to the measurement performed.

entities.name: quantization
entities.description: Restriction of physical quantities or energies to discrete allowable values.

entities.name: quantum electrodynamics
entities.description: Quantum field theory of the electromagnetic force.
aliases: quantum theory of the electromagnetic force

entities.name: quantum entanglement
entities.description: Condition in which the quantum state of particles cannot be described independently, including when they are widely separated.

entities.name: quantum field
entities.description: Field treated within quantum theory, including the electromagnetic field whose quantum is the photon.

entities.name: quantum field theory
entities.description: Quantum theory of fields that permits particle creation and annihilation.

entities.name: quantum mechanics
entities.description: Study and theory of matter and its interactions with energy at atomic and subatomic scales.

entities.name: quantum revolution
entities.description: The shift from classical physical models to quantum mechanics prompted by phenomena classical physics could not explain.

entities.name: quantum tunneling
entities.description: Quantum process allowing electrons to penetrate a potential barrier.

entities.name: Rydberg formula
entities.description: Formula predicting the distinctive absorption-line frequencies of hydrogen gas.

entities.name: spin
entities.description: Quantum degree of freedom associated with electrons and discrete magnetic behavior of atoms.

entities.name: Standard Model
entities.description: Quantum field theory describing three fundamental forces and classifying known elementary particles.

entities.name: Stern–Gerlach experiment
entities.description: Experiment in which a beam of atoms separates into two streams in a magnetic field, demonstrating quantized spin states.

entities.name: superconductor
entities.description: Macroscopic quantum phenomenon and technological application of quantum mechanics.

entities.name: superfluidity
entities.description: Quantum phenomenon in which liquid helium near absolute zero spontaneously flows up and over its container rim.

entities.name: transistor
entities.description: Quantum-mechanical technological component used in modern electronics.

entities.name: uncertainty principle
entities.description: Principle that certain properties, such as position and momentum, cannot be simultaneously measured or defined to arbitrary precision.

entities.name: wave function
entities.description: Quantum description of a system's probabilistic or potential state.

entities.name: wave function collapse
entities.description: Conversion of a probabilistic quantum state into a definite measured value through measurement.

entities.name: wave–particle duality
entities.description: Principle that photons and matter exhibit both wave-like and particle-like behavior, neither classical description being sufficient alone.

aliases: quantum theory of the electromagnetic force
